svg.title: In-process ABV architecture within the tenant and application boundary
svg.desc: A reusable CLI calls an application interface and in-process facade. A coordinator obtains consistent provider evidence and runs administrative authorization and authority-boundary validation before committing. SQLite implements the provider now; PostgreSQL is planned later. All operations require the tenant and application pair. Failure produces no write.
svg.text: ABV: local request flow and storage boundary
Proposed implementation · in process · no HTTP or RPC
Mandatory outer context: tenant + application
Every entry and provider access checks the pair. Inner scope cannot widen it.
Reusable CLI command layer
Parse input · present output · no rules or SQL
Application interface → in-process facade
ABV library remains independent of CLI
Mutation coordinator: consistent validation + save
Acquire provider transaction protection; load evidence
Registered definitions via installation + this area's authority graph
Authorization evaluator adapter
May this caller perform this write
within its administrative scope?
Authority-boundary validator
Does proposed authority stay within
valid definitions, sources and lineage?
Both pass → persist exact proposal → commit → receipt
Rejection, error or conflict → no committed mutation
No reusable “validation ticket”; provider protection spans evidence reads through commit.
Transaction-aware storage provider interface
SQLite · first implementation
PostgreSQL · later provider
Shared application catalogs are accessed through validated context, not cloned per tenant.
Local testing uses explicit disposable fixtures. Production administrative authorization is a later integration.
